repos/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/pu.body:
The reviewers, the use session and the criterion readers read the first head at which the planned build is done and the floor passes; their findings are answered in one batch; and the cold reading runs after that batch, once, holding only proof and the release report.

Built on the builder route from the [settled plan](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/issues/1014#issuecomment-7153192615) under the [affirmed brief](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/issues/1014#issuecomment-7153014506). This change itself ran on the order in force before it, as the brief's Delivery paragraph says.

**Waiting on you:** nothing -- no ask is marked on this change.

## What changed

- **The order** (`lib/work.py`, `_owed_before_reading`). After the floor, on both routes and every lane: the ready step; on the builder route each criterion or row reader with no counting report; the first use on the pull request; the reviewers and their answers; a relay use that changed something; a bought panel; then the cold reading, use again where no use evidence stands at the head, proof and release. The cold reading holds only `proof` and `release-report`. `run cold-reader` refuses `cold-reading-not-yet-owed`, naming the stage to take first, while anything before it is owed, and refuses while the route can't be read. On the relay route the first fix stage's detail and the reading's `before_reading` carry the wait for the criterion readers the entrance can't read.
- **The handoff** (`lib/handoff.py`): fourteen steps in that order, one step that answers every report in one batch (a catch-up doesn't wait; a second look may be bought and is recorded), and each hold sentence true of the entrance.
- **The release report** gains `reviewers_read` (`lib/reviewers_read.py`): the head first marked ready (from the timeline), how long after the build began, cold readings before it, whether a fix came before the last report (`true` / `false` / `unknown`), whether the first reading followed the fix batch, and what changed after, with a one-line sentence.
- **The comparison** records each change's order (`reviewers-first` / `cold-reading-first` / `unknown`) and lists `entries`; the count is not restarted.
- **Doctrine**: what marking ready means is stated once in `connected-reviewers.md` and pointed at from the stretch and release-report references; every sentence that depended on the earlier order is brought in line; `lib/DESIGN.md` and decision entry D-1030.
- Version 0.220.0 → 0.221.0.

## Existing tests rewritten, and why

- `test_handoff.py`: `test_1011_owed_checks_order_and_shape`, `test_1011_every_command_names_repo_issue_and_holder_root_and_no_session_id`, `test_1011_the_closing_line_and_who_posts_the_cold_reading`, `test_the_steps_render_in_their_fixed_order_with_their_holds`, `test_the_resolve_step_names_resolving_each_answered_thread_and_when_it_is_owed`, `test_the_floor_runs_again_after_a_later_commit_before_proof` — the steps, their holds and the owed checks are in the new order.
- `test_cold_reader.py`: the `Change` fixture reads a ready pull request its reviewer has read, since the reading now follows both; six assertions that a clean reading leads to `ready-reviewers` now lead to `proof`; `test_a_named_stage_the_gate_holds_refuses_without_effect` covers only `proof` and `release-report`; `test_a_settled_artifact_lane_is_gated_and_resumes_its_builder` posts the first use before the reading.
- `test_builder_route_walk.py`: `test_a_builder_taking_the_handoffs_steps_in_order_is_led_to_ready_reported` walks the new order.
- `test_builder_route_release_report.py`: `test_a_hand_started_builders_stretch_reads_not_applicable_and_its_owed_checks_come_from_the_hand_record` — the owed list now leads with reach held on the ready step.
- `test_after_ready.py`: `ready_hand` stands in for the criterion reports its record names.
- `test_work.py`: `test_reviewers_precede_use_and_proof_on_every_lane` becomes `test_use_and_the_reviewers_read_the_first_build_before_a_panel_and_proof_on_every_lane`; `test_raw_output_inventory_failure_refuses_ready_use_and_panel_routing` gives the panel lane its first use; `test_each_state_table_row_routes_exactly_one_stage` (a use with `changed=true` on a draft now reads the ready step); `test_mechanical_lane_keeps_dispositions_and_release_report`, `test_undisposed_reviewer_thread_routes_only_the_disposition_stage`, `test_938_an_empty_reply_block_names_no_holder_step` (the relay first fix's detail carries the batch sentence); `test_bought_use_returns_an_actionable_holder_handoff`, `test_use_handoff_names_registered_implementation_root_and_revision` (`pull-request-use-absent`).
- `test_work_version.py`: `test_C3_C5_ready_use_recommends_required_version_repair_first` (`pull-request-use-absent`).
- `test_change_cost.py`: two comparison tests compare the result without its new `entries`.
- `test_route_fixture.py`: `test_list_names_every_scenario` and `test_each_scenario_prints_the_decision_it_names` take the new scenarios.

New: `test_check_order.py`, `test_reviewers_read.py`, and tests in the walk, after-ready, change-cost and route-fixture suites.

## Decisions

- On the builder route an owed list nobody can read holds no reading (the final pass names it), and an accounting of the builder's checks that can't be read holds every owed reader.
- On the relay mechanical lane the brief rows' readers are listed as unread in the release report.
- A catch-up merge counts as bringing in the base only where its combined diff is empty, read without writing objects.
- The first reading followed the fix batch only where it was launched once every report on the ready head was in.
- Declined from the second use session: its fifteen findings, each with its reason in the readiness record.
- Declined from the reviewers: holding the reading on answers to use and criterion findings (the brief's row 3 makes it owed once they have reported); a field for a second look (named by whoever writes the report); restarting a builder in its recorded copy's order (C7 and row 6 keep the recorded root and build no move).

**Path departures:** this change ran on the order in force before it (cold reading before the ready step), as its brief's Delivery paragraph says. The builder's stretch stopped while waiting on the reviewers and the holder resumed it ("Resume it"). Nine cold readings ran: one reader's return failed the form check and was run again, the pre-launch cap was raised to 2,400 s with its reason because the reach read outran the 900 s default, and three flags across the fifth and ninth readings were accepted with reasons. The first use session's return ran past its findings list, so the entrance counts it as one finding (`F0`). The fix batch answered the reviewers and the first use session together; the use session ran again at the final head, and its fifteen findings, which describe behaviour that predates this change or the stand-in states' limits, are declined in the readiness record with reasons. One Ubuntu floor run failed a Linux-only timing test this change doesn't touch (`test_978_stream_bound_reaches_an_escapee_adopted_after_the_stop`), and the next push's floor passed.

Closes #1014

This change reorders review so reviewers, use and criterion readers read the first complete build, and the cold reading follows the batched answers. A builder restarted from an earlier installation can be given the new step order while its commands still enforce the old one, which can stall it. The cold reading can also start before findings from use and criterion reports are answered. The new reviewers-read section of the release report can state the order or fix timing incorrectly in edge cases. Resolve the restart mismatch and the composed-findings gap before merging, and fix the report inaccuracies soon after.

```python
"""Per merged pull request: how long it sat before its reviewers, and what each check found when.

Read-only. Every figure comes from GitHub: the pull request, its timeline, its commits, its review
comments, and the cold-reading markers on the issue it implements.

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime

OWNER = "Grimblaz-and-Friends"
SINCE = "2026-11-06"  # the cold reader's gate landed on 2026-11-05 (plugin 0.206.0)
MARK = re.compile(r"<!-- tradecraft:cold-reading:v1 head=([0-9a-f]{40}) status=(open|clean)")


def gh(*args):
    done = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8")
    if done.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"gh {' '.join(args)}: {done.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
    return done.stdout


def paged(path):
    out = gh("api", path, "--paginate", "--slurp")
    return [row for page in json.loads(out) for row in page]


def when(text):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace("Z", "+00:00")) if text else None


def hours(a, b):
    return None if a is None or b is None else round((b - a).total_seconds() / 3600, 1)


def issue_of(pr):
    body = pr.get("body") or ""
    found = re.search(r"(?im)^\s*(?:closes|fixes|resolves)\s+#(\d+)\s*$", body)
    if found:
        return int(found.group(1))
    found = re.findall(r"\(#(\d+)\)", pr["title"])
    return int(found[0]) if found else None


def measure(repo, number):
    base = f"repos/{OWNER}/{repo}"
    pr = json.loads(gh("api", f"{base}/pulls/{number}"))
    created, merged = when(pr["created_at"]), when(pr["merged_at"])
    events = paged(f"{base}/issues/{number}/timeline?per_page=100")
    readies = [when(e["created_at"]) for e in events if e.get("event") == "ready_for_review"]
    ready = min(readies) if readies else None
    commits = paged(f"{base}/pulls/{number}/commits?per_page=100")
    shas = {c["sha"] for c in commits}
    pushes = [when(e["created_at"]) for e in events if e.get("event") in ("head_ref_force_pushed",)]
    comments = paged(f"{base}/pulls/{number}/comments?per_page=100")
    bot_inline = [c for c in comments if c["user"]["type"] == "Bot" and not c.get("in_reply_to_id")]
    first_bot = min((when(c["created_at"]) for c in bot_inline), default=None)
    issue = issue_of(pr)
    before = after = None
    if issue is not None and ready is not None:
        try:
            notes = paged(f"{base}/issues/{issue}/comments?per_page=100")
        except RuntimeError:
            notes = []
```

### G1. One order, decided in one place

The cold-reading gate moves inside `chain`, and neither caller asks it ahead of `chain`. After the floor, a change is given its stages in this order on every route and lane:

1. **The ready step.** A draft pull request reads `ready-reviewers`, as today. Reach holds it, as today.
2. **The criterion readers, where the entrance can read them.** On the builder route, an owed criterion reader, or on the mechanical lane an owed row reader, with no counting report from this term's builder reads as owed, naming each one. `handoff.owed_checks` says which are owed.
3. **The first use report.** Where use is bought and no use evidence stands for any commit the pull request holds, the decision reads `use`.
4. **The reviewers.** A configured reviewer that has not run reads `waiting`, as today.
5. **The answers.** A thread or body finding with no disposition reads `review-disposition`, then an answered thread left unresolved, as today.
6. **A use that changed something, on the relay route.** P4's check moves here from in front of the gate, so it no longer returns the builder before the reviewers have run.
7. **A bought panel,** where it sits today relative to the answers and proof.
8. **The cold reading.** `_cold_reading_decision`, unchanged inside: what a reading covers, how a flag is accepted, when a reread is owed and what it covers, and what counts as `clean` all stay as they are.
9. **Use at the head.** Today's rule: where no use evidence stands at the head or at an ancestor the use rules accept, the decision reads `use`.
10. **Proof, the gate, the merge verdict and the release report,** as today.

Steps 3 and 9 are two questions. Step 3 asks whether a use has reported on this pull request at all, so the reviewers, use and the criterion readers read the same first build and the fix batch has every report. Step 9 asks today's question, so a use made stale by the fix batch or by the reading's fixes runs once, after the reading is clean.

A catch-up with the base keeps its place in front of all of this (`_synchronization_decision`), so it never waits on a report.

### G3. The handoff's text follows the entrance

`BUILDER_STEPS` takes this order, and `owed_checks` and `CHECK_STEPS` follow it:

1. open the pull request;
2. the floor;
3. reach;
4. the ready step;
5. the criterion readers;

## 2. The decisions

### G1. One order, decided in one place

The cold-reading gate moves inside `chain`, and neither caller asks it ahead of `chain`. After the floor, a change is given its stages in this order on every route and lane:

1. **The ready step.** A draft pull request reads `ready-reviewers`, as today. Reach holds it, as today.
2. **The criterion readers, where the entrance can read them.** On the builder route, an owed criterion reader, or on the mechanical lane an owed row reader, with no counting report from this term's builder reads as owed, naming each one. `handoff.owed_checks` says which are owed.
3. **The first use report.** Where use is bought and no use evidence stands for any commit the pull request holds, the decision reads `use`.
4. **The reviewers.** A configured reviewer that has not run reads `waiting`, as today.
5. **The answers.** A thread or body finding with no disposition reads `review-disposition`, then an answered thread left unresolved, as today.
6. **A use that changed something, on the relay route.** P4's check moves here from in front of the gate, so it no longer returns the builder before the reviewers have run.
7. **A bought panel,** where it sits today relative to the answers and proof.
8. **The cold reading.** `_cold_reading_decision`, unchanged inside: what a reading covers, how a flag is accepted, when a reread is owed and what it covers, and what counts as `clean` all stay as they are.
9. **Use at the head.** Today's rule: where no use evidence stands at the head or at an ancestor the use rules accept, the decision reads `use`.
10. **Proof, the gate, the merge verdict and the release report,** as today.

Steps 3 and 9 are two questions. Step 3 asks whether a use has reported on this pull request at all, so the reviewers, use and the criterion readers read the same first build and the fix batch has every report. Step 9 asks today's question, so a use made stale by the fix batch or by the reading's fixes runs once, after the reading is clean.

A catch-up with the base keeps its place in front of all of this (`_synchronization_decision`), so it never waits on a report.

On the relay route the entrance does not read criterion reports (P6), so step 2 names no stage there. The requirement still binds there, and the entrance says so at the two decisions a relay holder acts on after the reports:

- the ready step's detail (`_draft_ready_detail`) stops asking for the holder's account of the criteria;
- the first fix stage after the ready step, `review-disposition` or the `build` that step 6 returns, says in its detail that the holder first has the use report and every criterion reader's report, and sends their findings with the reviewers' in one turn;
- the decision that orders a reading says in its detail that every criterion reader has reported and its findings are answered, and that the holder's account of the criteria is recorded, before the reader runs.

So on the relay route the holder's account of the criteria sits before the cold reading, as row 3 has it, where today it sits before the ready step. The doctrine says so too (G6). This is a call inside rows 1, 2 and 3, recorded in section 8.

### G2. What a named stage is refused

- `COLD_READING_HELD_STAGES` becomes `proof` and `release-report`. `run ready-reviewers`, `run use`, and a composed use or criterion check no longer ask the gate, whether the reading is missing, `open` or stale.
- `run cold-reader` refuses, launching nothing, while anything in G1's steps 1 to 7 is owed. The refusal names the stage and reason owed first, in words a builder holding an older handoff text can act on. Without this a builder or holder naming the stage would put the reading back in front, and row 3's order would hold only for a session that followed the recommendation. On the relay route the refusal cannot see a criterion reader, so there the requirement travels in the detail of the decision that orders the reading (G1).
- `run proof` and `run release-report` refuse `cold-reading-holds` exactly as today.

### G3. The handoff's text follows the entrance

`BUILDER_STEPS` takes this order, and `owed_checks` and `CHECK_STEPS` follow it:

1. open the pull request;
2. the floor;
3. reach;
4. the ready step;
5. the criterion readers;
6. use, where it is owed;
7. answer the findings: one step that waits for every required reviewer's review, the use report and every criterion report, then fixes or declines every finding of all of them in one batch. It says that a catch-up with the base is not a fix and does not wait;
8. the floor again;
9. resolve the answered threads;
10. the cold reader, until a `clean` stands;
11. use again, only where the decision names it;
12. proof;
13. the readiness record;
14. read the record back.

Each step the entrance holds carries a sentence naming that hold, and each sentence is true of the entrance: the ready step is named once the floor stands and held until reach is settled; the cold reader is refused until the reports are in and the findings answered; proof is held until a `clean` reading stands at the head and reach is settled there. `ANSWERS` and `BUILDER_MODE_REASONS` gain every reason G1 and G2 add, each tied to the step that answers it.

The step that answers the findings also says that the builder may buy a second reviewer look by the connected-reviewer rule, and records one it buys in its readiness record's `decisions`.

### G4. The release report says what the reviewers read

`run release-report` adds one section to its payload on both routes, named for what it holds (the builder chooses the key). It carries:

- **the head the reviewers read:** the pull request's head when it was first marked ready, read from the pull request's timeline on GitHub as the last commit before the first `ready_for_review` event. Where a required reviewer's first review names another commit, the section names that reviewer and commit as well;
- **how long after the build began that was:** the ready step's time less the launch time of the term's first builder launch (`build` or `stretch`), in seconds;
- **how many cold readings came before it:** the cold-reader launches for this pull request started before the ready step;
- **whether any fix was pushed before the last report on that head:** true where a commit after that head, other than a merge that brings in the base, is dated before the last of the first use report, each criterion report the entrance can read, and each required reviewer's first review. The section names the commit, and says it compared committer dates;
- **the first cold reading:** its head, and whether that head follows the commits that answered the findings;
- **what changed after:** each file changed between that head and the report's head with its added and removed lines, and the total, from `git diff --numstat` between the two commits. Where the two are one commit it says nothing changed after.

Each part the entrance cannot read says `unknown` with its reason and never a guessed value: an unreadable timeline, a pull request never a draft, no builder launch on record, a commit the holder's objects lack.

The timeline is read only by `run release-report`, so the ordinary decision gains no GitHub read.

### G7. A change in flight

Nothing is migrated. The entrance reads a change's state and gives the new order from wherever the change stands, so a clean reading already at the head is kept and nothing is redone.

That holds for every decision made through the updated practice: the holder's, and that of a builder handed off after this lands, which takes the new order from its handoff text.

```text
You are carrying a product change in a repository that has adopted the tradecraft practice, and the tree in front of you is that practice at the head of a change to it. At each of these moments say what you would do next and why, what you may not do yet and how you know, and where the material fought you: what you had to guess, what contradicted itself, or what you could not find.

1. The code is written, pushed and passing its checks in CI, and nothing has looked at it yet.
2. Other parties are looking at it, and some have reported.
3. Everything that looked at it has reported, with findings.
4. The findings are answered and pushed.
5. You are about to tell the owner the change is theirs to merge.

B. The owner asks whether the reviewers saw the code they are about to merge. Where do they find that, and what does it say?
C. A step you were told to take later is refused when you try it. What do you do?

Return what you ran and saw at each moment. End with a section `Findings:` listing each problem as `F<n>. ...`, or `Findings: none`.
```

The cold-reading gate moves inside `chain`, and neither caller asks it ahead of `chain`. After the floor, a change is given its stages in this order on every route and lane:

3. **The first use report.** Where use is bought and no use evidence stands for any commit the pull request holds, the decision reads `use`.
4. **The reviewers.** A configured reviewer that has not run reads `waiting`, as today.
5. **The answers.** A thread or body finding with no disposition reads `review-disposition`, then an answered thread left unresolved, as today.
6. **A use that changed something, on the relay route.** P4's check moves here from in front of the gate, so it no longer returns the builder before the reviewers have run.

9. **Use at the head.** Today's rule: where no use evidence stands at the head or at an ancestor the use rules accept, the decision reads `use`.
10. **Proof, the gate, the merge verdict and the release report,** as today.

Steps 3 and 9 are two questions. Step 3 asks whether a use has reported on this pull request at all, so the reviewers, use and the criterion readers read the same first build and the fix batch has every report. Step 9 asks today's question, so a use made stale by the fix batch or by the reading's fixes runs once, after the reading is clean.

A catch-up with the base keeps its place in front of all of this (`_synchronization_decision`), so it never waits on a report.

## Use session job

```text
You are carrying a product change in a repository that has adopted the tradecraft practice, and the tree in front of you is that practice at the head of a change to it. Run every command with `python -B`, and write only in the folder around the tree or in your session scratchpad; leave the tree as built.

`lib/tests/route_fixture.py` can put the practice into stand-in states of a product change; its `--list` names them, and you may run any of them by those names.

Work through the life of one change after its code is first written, twice: once as the session that builds it and gets it ready, and once as the session that designed it with the owner and reports it to them. Use the tree's own material and whichever stand-in states you choose. At each of these moments say what you would do next and why, what you may not do yet and how you know, and where the material fought you: what you had to guess, what contradicted itself, or what you could not find.

1. The code is written, pushed and passing its checks in CI, and nothing has looked at it yet.
2. Other parties are looking at it, and some have reported.
3. Everything that looked at it has reported, with findings.
4. The findings are answered and pushed.
5. You are about to tell the owner the change is theirs to merge.

Then answer three questions from the material alone, quoting what you rely on:

A. A teammate sees your change's pull request showing as ready for review. What does that tell them, and what does it not tell them?
B. The owner asks whether the reviewers saw the code they are about to merge. Where do they find that, and what does it say?
C. A step you were told to take later is refused when you try it. What do you do?
```

## 8. Calls made inside the rows, with reasons

1. **A named reading is refused before its turn (G2).** Row 3 says when the reading is owed. Leaving `run cold-reader` launchable from the floor on would keep the old order one command away.
2. **The first use and the use at the head are two questions (G1, steps 3 and 9).** One question would either run use twice whenever the fix batch touches a shipped path, or let the fix batch start without a use report.
3. **On the relay route the criterion readers' turn is carried by the decisions' own words (G1).** The entrance reads use and the reviewers there, not criterion reports, and building a relay-route record of them is a mechanism the brief did not buy. So the ask that rides the ready step today moves to the first fix stage and to the decision that orders the reading, and the holder's account of the criteria sits before the cold reading. For the same reason the release report's fix field reads `unknown` there for a change that owes a criterion reader, and never `false` (G4).
4. **A relay-route use that changed something waits for the reviewers (G1, step 6).** It is a fix, and row 2 says the first fix waits.
5. **The reviewers' head is read from the timeline (G4),** because it needs no new record and covers a pull request made ready by hand. A reviewer whose first review names another commit is named beside it.
6. **A change's order is read from what happened to it (G5):** whether a cold reading came before its ready step. A change in flight at landing is then named by the order it in fact ran under.
7. **An older ledger entry is listed as the earlier order (G5),** because it was written when no other order existed.
8. **Thread resolution comes before the cold reader in the builder's steps (G3),** because the entrance names it straight after the answers.
9. **The release report's sentence sits directly after "Needs your decision" (G6),** so the owner sees how much followed the reviewers' look without opening the collapsed section, which is what lets them buy a second look where it is large.
10. **A copy moved under its builder is the one case where a builder's order changes mid-run (G7).** Row 6's builder cell says a builder finishes on the copy its handoff named, in that copy's order, and its adopter cell says a builder still running when they update finishes on the order it started with. An adopter's update installs a new copy beside the named one, so both sentences say the same thing there. Where the named copy is a working checkout that is moved, which is this repository's own arrangement, the builder cell's words decide it: the copy's order is then the new one, and the decision and the refusals lead the builder to it (C7). The adopter cell's sentence is read as speaking of an installed copy.
11. **The later change's checks are read by the lab's coordinating session (C14),** because this change's holder and builder have ended by then, and the brief says only that they are read from that change's release report.

## Why this change was made
Can tell: yes
From `docs/architecture/decisions/D-1030-2026-11-25-reviewers-and-use-read-the-first-complete-build.md` ("Why the reviewers go first", "Nobody had decided the earlier order") and the Why bullets in `lib/DESIGN.md#the-cold-reader`:
- The reviewers are the check that finds defects, so they should read the first complete build.
- The cold reading goes stale at every push, and its fixes are mostly comments and documents, the smallest changes to leave for last.
- So the reading moves after one batch of answers and holds only proof and the release report.
- The earlier order was never decided; it came from placing a single hold point.

- `lib/work.py:5865-5919`: `_owed_before_reading` is the single order that both the decision's chain and `run cold-reader` ask, on every route and lane.
- `lib/work.py:6510-6541`: the builder-route final pass now splices per-reader entries and a reach hold into `owed_at_ready`, and `owed_chain` keeps only the first reader.
- `lib/work.py:13919-13931`: the relay route's unread-reader list leaves out the mechanical lane, which can turn the fix field into `false` where the design says `unknown`.
- `lib/work.py:13889-13892`: the count of cold readings before ready decides each change's order in the comparison ledger, yet it skips form-refused launches.
- `lib/reviewers_read.py:217-275`: the committer-date logic behind "a fix before the last report" and "followed the answers" is what the owner's one-line sentence rests on.

# Walking one change through tradecraft 0.221.0, as builder and as holder

I could walk both sessions through all five moments from the tree's own material. I found 11 problems. The two that matter most:

- **A hand-started builder's term can end by accident.** A holder command that the entrance refuses still closes the builder's record first.
- **The builder can't see its next step.** Until it posts a readiness record, the entrance's decision gives the builder nothing between handoff and ready.

All findings are listed at the end.

The tree was never written to. After all runs, every file's hash and mtime match a baseline I took before the first run, and `git status --porcelain --ignored` is empty. One footprint came before the baseline: my first `git status` on the tree moved the `.git` directory's own mtime to 07:37:19. It most likely created and removed an `index.lock`; `.git/index` itself is untouched (07:36:07). Every later git call used `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.

## A. The pull request shows "ready for review": what that tells a teammate

**It tells them:**
- "Marking a pull request ready for review means its planned build is complete and its floor passes, and nothing more" (connected-reviewers.md:7).
- It is the moment to review: "Its reviewers, and any teammate or code owner GitHub asks for a review, see it then, before its fix round, which is why it is marked then."

**It does not tell them:**
- That checks have passed or findings are settled: "it does not mean the practice's other checks have passed, and a fix round is expected to follow."
- That the change waits on its owner: "The release report is the one thing that says a change is waiting on its owner, so nobody is told a change is ready for its owner before the release report." The handoff says the same: "Ready means the planned build is complete and its reviewers may send it back, not that the other checks have passed."
- That the head will stay put. A fix round follows, and reviewers "fire once … never per push", so what they review may change after they read it.

The wording is slightly inconsistent elsewhere: work SKILL.md:145 and the-stretch.md:118 say "means only that the planned build is complete" (F7).

## B. Did the reviewers see the code the owner is about to merge?

**Where:** the release report, item 3, right after "Needs your decision": "**What the reviewers read.** One sentence, `run release-report`'s `reviewers_read.sentence`: which head the reviewers read and how much changed between it and the head the owner merges" (the-release-report.md:13). The full reading is under "Settled by checks" (item 7).

**What it says** in `reviewers-read`: "The reviewers read 41f2635, 16 minutes after the build began and after 0 cold readings; no fix was pushed before the last report on that head (compared by committer dates); no cold reading has been launched; 1 file and +1/-1 lines changed between it and ff6de0f, the head you merge." `changed_after` lists `job/job.md +1/-1`.

**So: not quite.** The reviewers saw the head first marked ready, not the fix that followed, and no second look was bought. The owner should check that the title line's "at head <sha>" is the head they merge.

The "0 cold readings / none launched" part reflects the fixture stubbing the reading. A real `run release-report` refuses until a `clean` reading stands.

## C. A step you were told to take later is refused when you try it. What do you do?

**Read the refusal; it names the step to take first, and you take that step.** "`run cold-reader` refuses `cold-reading-not-yet-owed`, launching nothing and naming the stage to take first … `run proof` and `run release-report` refuse without effect, naming the gate's stage and reason" (work SKILL.md:57). DESIGN.md:363: "the decision and the refusals, each naming the stage to take first, lead the builder to it." In `builder-reporting` the named step was `acceptance-criterion C2`.

**As the builder, record the refusal** under `refusals` ("the `command`, its `reason`, and what you did `then`"). Then read back: "Where it names only a wait … wait and read it again." Stop only by the stop rule: "Where a check cannot be launched, post `status=stopped` with a `cannot-launch` stop." A refused write is not retried: "the command fails and the turn goes on". I did the same when the guard refused my `xargs` pipeline.

**As the holder, a refusal tells you whose turn it is.** `with-builder` means wait. At `final-pass`, "the send-back is the holder's one remedy." The material's promise of "without effect" fails in one case: under a hand-started builder that has posted a record, the refused attempt itself ends the builder's term (F1).

F1. A holder `run` that is refused still ends a hand-started builder's term. Every holder-mode `run` calls `_complete_readied_hand_records` before `_refuse_off_route` and `_refuse_with_builder` (`work.py:14340-14345`). Once a hand-started builder posts its ready record, the read-only decision keeps reading `with-builder` and "hand-started record … is open, awaiting its readiness record or run handoff --ended-reason", while that record stands at the head (all four `builder-*` outputs, records 105–108). F4. `route_fixture.py:541-543` says the stand-in builder "posts its record at the head after each step, as the handoff's read-back says", and every `builder-*` moment posts a `status=ready` record. The handoff and markers.md:270 say the record is "the last thing you post at each ready report, after proof". **Owner ask and its answer: the builder stopped at its limit, and the owner said to resume it.**

This records an ask put to the owner in conversation, after the brief was affirmed.

- **What was asked.** The builder's first stretch ran its whole 28,800-second window and stopped at the limit without a ready record (dispatch `1c95e6544f2d402eb81fddb48565aa71`, stopped 2026-11-25T13:00:54Z). The holder asked whether to resume it or leave it stopped, and recommended resuming.
- **Which case applied.** Neither an affirmed row nor a saving: the practice gives the resume of a stopped builder to the owner's word, so the holder could not make this call. No affirmed row changes.
- **Where the change stood.** The pull request was open and ready at head `0700deb2898e20024f6bd5cf2825926cabc70ef4` with its floor green, the fifth cold reading clean, and one use session run. Fourteen reviewer comments were unanswered, and neither proof nor the ready record had been produced.
- **Stated cost.** One more builder window of up to 28,800 seconds; the holder's estimate for what remains was three to five hours. The cost report prices the eleven seat dispatches so far at about $21.96 at list and reads the first stretch as `unknown`, because an interrupted run returns no usage (#1031).
- **Route before the owner.** The holder told the Steward first. The Steward confirmed from the record that the resume is the owner's and that no ruling on #683 changes that.
- **The answer.** "Resume it" (2026-11-25T16:04:08Z).
- **Outcome.** `run handoff --resume-reason "Resume it"` was called at 2026-11-25T16:04:32Z and handed off: dispatch `70361169fa4d414e82dffaae269bbfbe`, resuming session `8c8ab76c-6fa7-4c82-b176-d6193d2c9af2`, limit 28,800 seconds at the default, latest return 2026-11-26T00:24:13Z.

## Why this change was made
Can tell: yes

From `lib/DESIGN.md` "The cold reader" (Why bullets at `:57-61`, in-force D-1030 at `:78`) and "The builder route" (`:378-379,382`).

- The reviewers are the check that finds defects, so they, use and the criterion readers read the first complete build, and their findings are answered in one batch.
- The cold reading goes stale at every push and its fixes are mostly comments and documents, so it runs last and holds only proof and the release report.
- The release report gains a section showing which head the reviewers read and how much changed after it, so the owner can buy a second look where that is large.
- The route comparison records the order each change ran under, and a running builder finishes on the copy of the practice its handoff named.

## Worth a look
- `lib/reviewers_read.py:318-320,369-370`: when `first_reading` is None, the section reports "no cold reading has been launched". But `work.py` builds `first_reading` from `_cold_readings`, which drops returns the form check refused, while `cold_readings_before` counts every launch. So the sentence can say "after 1 cold reading … no cold reading has been launched", which is the exact case in `test_check_order`'s test that a reading launched before the ready step counts whatever its return.
- `lib/work.py:13919-13945`: the launch count and the first reading come from two different sources with different lineage and form filters, and the launch time falls back to the completion time.
- `lib/work.py:5885-5940`: `_owed_before_reading` is the one order both the decision chain and `run cold-reader` use; the gate's new position rests entirely on it.
- `lib/work.py:6537-6571`: the final pass's owed list removes duplicates of chain readers, treats reach-read as an owed stage through `held_by_reach`, and replaces `chained` wholesale with the readers. It is dense, and the single-listing guarantee depends on it.
- `lib/work.py:6078-6101`: the named-reading refusal path. A reading whose route can't be read waits, and when no rules are passed, use counts as bought on every lane but the mechanical one.

The full section sits in the collapsed "Settled by checks". The reference never names the surface the report itself is posted on (F9).

**What it says** (`reviewers-read` stand-in): "The reviewers read 41f2635, 16 minutes after the build began and after 0 cold readings; whether a fix came before the last report is unknown: …; no cold reading has been launched; 1 file and +1/-1 lines changed between it and ff6de0f, the head you merge."

So the answer is **no**: one changed line in `job/job.md` followed the reviewers' only look.

**Caveats:**
- "The reviewers read" is the head at the first ready-for-review event (`reviewers_read.ready_head`), not proof that any reviewer reviewed. `ready-reported` prints the same sentence with no reviewer configured (F5).
- A bought second look, which the reference says belongs "in the same sentence", has no place in the generated sentence (F4).

## C. A step you were told to take later is refused when you try it

**As the builder:**
- Take the step the refusal names first; the order is the entrance's own. the-stretch.md:67: "the builder takes its steps in the entrance's own order, which is fixed wherever an entrance hold names the step before it."
- The SKILL says `run cold-reader` refuses "naming the stage to take first", and `run proof`/`run release-report` refuse "naming the gate's stage and reason".
- Record the refusal. Handoff: "`refusals`: each command the entrance refused you: the `command`, its `reason`, and what you did `then`."
- If the reason is launch findings, "post their launch-account first". If it "names only a wait … wait and read it again".
- If the reason means stop, follow the stop rule (the-stretch.md:84): "a reason the entrance returns that means stop points at that rule." The reasons that mean stop are listed only in DESIGN: `builder-stopped`, `cannot-launch`, `affirmed-brief-marker-absent`.
- A refused GitHub write: "the command fails and the turn goes on". A write the brief doesn't name "goes to the owner as a change to an affirmed row".

**As the holder:**
- While the builder is live, stay quiet.
- At the final pass, the refusal names the remedy: "send the builder back once instead". the-stretch.md:104: "the send-back is the holder's one remedy … because every owed stage is the builder's."

**Caution:** the builder may be pointed at a stage it can't run (F3). Before the record exists it reads `builder-stopped`, which maps to stop (F1).

Findings:
F1. Before its one readiness record, a live builder's read-only decision never gives its next step. At moments 1, 3 and 4 (`norecord.py`) it reads `with-builder` with `if_ended: stretch-stopped / builder-stopped`, and `handoff.ANSWERS` maps `builder-stopped` to the stop step. The `builder-*` scenarios hide this by posting a stand-in ready record at every moment, which their own docstring says a real builder doesn't do.
F2. Handoff step 7 says "the read-only decision names any [connected reviewer] not yet run", but before the record exists the builder's decision names no reviewer state at all.
F3. The entrance names `review-disposition` to the builder: in `if_ended.owed_at_ready` at `builder-reported`, and in the cold-reader refusal ("take review-disposition (reviewer-thread-lacks-disposition) first. 501"). The builder may not run that stage (not in `BUILDER_STAGES`), and the composed handoff names neither it nor `reviewer-thread-lacks-disposition`. The step it means is mapped only in `handoff.ANSWERS` code.
F4. the-release-report.md item 3 and connected-reviewers.md:11 say a bought second reviewer look is named in `reviewers_read.sentence` with what it found. `reviewers_read.first_reviews` keeps only each reviewer's first review, and `_sentence` has no clause for a second look.
F5. `reviewers_read.sentence` opens "The reviewers read <sha>" from the first ready-for-review event, not from any reviewer's review. `ready-reported`, with no connected reviewer configured, still tells the owner "The reviewers read 41f2635".
F6. The final-pass decision ignores `readiness.launched_by_builder`. In `reviewers-read` it is `false` (the record's use check head `ff6de0f` ≠ report 104's head `41f2635`, so row check 1.2 fails), yet the decision reads `final-pass`/`ready-reported`, and the-stretch.md's final-pass reading list doesn't point the holder at it.
F7. The `reviewers-read` stand-in (`ready_launched(fixed=True)`) writes a readiness record naming its use check at the fix head, though the use report read the head marked ready. The scenario models a record the handoff's own contract ("the full commit `head` it read") makes wrong.
F8. Every moment-5 stand-in (`final-pass`, `ready-reported`, `reviewers-read`) has a handoff block with no `owed_checks`. So `owed_list`, `owed_at_ready.first/last`, row check 1.1 and `fix_before_last_report` all read `unknown`, and the final pass can't be walked with an owed list.
F9. No file in the tree says where the release report is posted (issue or pull request). the-release-report.md gives its title line and order only, so the owner can be told only "in the release report".
F10. The relay holder's way to launch use and criterion readers disagrees across surfaces. The relay `use` decision says "dispatch the consumer through lib/dispatch_seat.py", and the-stretch.md:118 says readers go "through `lib/dispatch_seat.py`". The work SKILL says `run use --dispatch JOB --tree-metadata RECORD`, and the entrance's refusal text says "the holder launches criteria by --criterion".
F11. Every report's `route` carries a `chosen` field (`default`, `unasked`), and release-report row check 7.2 reasons on it ("chosen default"). The work SKILL's description of `route` omits it, and I found `unasked` documented nowhere.
F12. A hand-started builder's record is reported under `launch_findings` as `not recorded: launched before #906`. launch-findings.md:46 reserves that for "A bundle recorded before this bound", but this record was written by the current writer and never launched.
F13. The work SKILL says "while a builder of the term is live, every holder-mode `run` is refused `with-builder`". With a live builder, the entrance refused `run ready-reviewers` as `stage-is-the-builders` and `run review-disposition` as `route-is-builder`, and the material doesn't say which reason applies when both do.
F14. "How to finish" in the composed handoff says "read your record back with the reach check's command", naming the read-only decision by the reach step. Step 14 names it directly, so the two sentences describe one command two ways.
F15. No named stand-in takes the relay route past its fourth moment (no proof, ready or release-report state). Naming `run release-report` at `relay-answered` stops on "route fixture: GitHub get is not served beyond the issue's records", so the relay holder's moment 5 can't be walked with the fixture.
